reasons: The 'Doctor Verified' badge is always shown, which claims a clinical check that the code does not perform.
No test is visible for how the card handles missing or unexpected input.

terms.meaning: a number showing how sure the AI is about its summary, here shown as a percentage
a method where an AI looks up relevant documents before it writes an answer
the information a parent component passes into a child component
a written description of the shape of data a component expects

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the summary card
sections.what: Brings in the React library, icons, the card component, and a helper for combining styles. Nothing appears on screen from this section.
sections.why: The card needs these pieces to draw itself.

sections.name: AISummaryProps
sections.title: Data the card expects
sections.what: Defines the four pieces of data the card needs: the summary text, a list of findings, a list of recommendations, and a confidence number.
sections.why: Makes the expected input clear so the parent component passes the right shape.
sections.watch_out: Nothing here checks the data at run time, so a wrong shape from the parent will cause display errors.

sections.name: AISummaryCard (part 1)
sections.title: Summary header and summary text
sections.what: Shows the card heading, the confidence percentage, a 'Clinical RAG Active' label, a 'Doctor Verified' label, and the main summary text.
sections.why: Gives the summary context and shows how sure the AI is.
sections.watch_out: The 'Doctor Verified' label is always visible, so it claims a review that the code does not verify.

sections.name: AISummaryCard (part 2)
sections.title: Key observations, next steps and disclaimer
sections.what: Shows the key findings and the next steps as two bulleted lists side by side. A footer notes that the summary is informational and a physician must make any diagnosis.
sections.why: Separates what the AI noticed from what it suggests doing next, and reminds users that it is not a diagnosis.
sections.watch_out: The lists assume each item is a short string, so an object in the list would show incorrectly.

summary: A card that shows an AI-written clinical summary with confidence, key observations, and next steps, using the data it is given.
purpose: Presents a patient-friendly AI summary of health records on the dashboard or a report page.
why: Gives the patient a readable overview of the AI's findings, along with a disclaimer that a doctor should be consulted.
how: It receives the summary text, a list of findings, a list of next steps, and a confidence number. It shows the confidence as a percentage, then the summary, then the two lists side by side, and finally a disclaimer footer.
inputs: A summary text, a list of key findings, a list of recommendations, and a confidence number between 0 and 1.
outputs: A visual card with the summary, two lists, a confidence percentage, and a disclaimer.
risks: The labels 'Doctor Verified' and 'Clinical RAG Active' are always shown, even when no doctor has checked the summary and no retrieval step was used. This can overstate the reliability of the output.
debug: If the percentage looks wrong, check that the confidence value is between 0 and 1 when it arrives. If the lists are empty, check the data passed in from the parent component.
